title: Event-Driven Audit and Evidence Ledger
summary: Provide immutable, project-scoped and integrity-verifiable event and evidence records for governed engineering operations.

intent.statement: Ensure that every material engineering action, decision, agent operation, verification result and runtime observation can be reconstructed through immutable, project-scoped evidence.
desired_outcomes: Audit history is reconstructable without mutable log assumptions.
Evidence distinguishes observed results from unverified assertions.
Consumers receive durable internal events without weakening authoritative integrity.

success_measures.name: Ledger provenance coverage
success_measures.target: 100% of governed P0/P2 material actions emit a scoped, versioned event
success_measures.measurement_method: Reconcile domain command audit requirements against appended event types.

success_measures.name: Integrity verification success
success_measures.target: No undetected sequence or hash mismatch in controlled ledger verification tests
success_measures.measurement_method: Run gap, tamper and replay fixtures through integrity verifier.

out_of_scope: Raw secret or private reasoning storage.

provenance.rationale: Derived from AGASTYA evidence, auditability and production-reconciliation principles.

problem.statement: Engineering systems cannot establish trust when events, approvals, test results and agent actions are held only in mutable logs or disconnected tools.
problem.current_state: AGASTYA defines audit and evidence requirements but has no unified append-only event envelope, integrity chain, transactional outbox or evidence-record contract.
impact: Approvals and verification claims may not be reconstructable.
Downstream projections can diverge from authoritative domain state.
Sensitive payloads may be retained inconsistently without classification controls.

business_context.business_value: A durable Evidence Ledger is the common proof layer connecting intent, implementation, verification, policy and production behaviour.

stakeholders.name: Platform Engineering
stakeholders.role: Owns ledger runtime and event delivery

stakeholders.name: Engineering Governance
stakeholders.role: Owns audit, retention and integrity policy

actors.name: Registered Domain Producer
goals: Append valid governed audit and evidence events.

actors.name: Authorised Project Reviewer
goals: Inspect project-scoped audit and evidence history.

functional_requirements.title: Append canonical audit events
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall append schema-valid project-scoped audit events with immutable identity, type version, producer, actor, subject, correlation, causation, classification and integrity metadata.

functional_requirements.title: Append evidence records
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall append evidence records that identify expected and observed behaviour, exact subject versions, truth state, provenance, classification and artefact hash/reference.

provenance.rationale: Evidence must be distinct from assertions.

functional_requirements.title: Enforce append-only integrity chain
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall allocate monotonic project sequence numbers and hash-chain each ledger record in the same transaction as the governed domain operation.

functional_requirements.title: Publish events through transactional outbox
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall persist an outbox record with the domain and ledger records, then support at-least-once internal delivery and idempotent consumer processing.

functional_requirements.title: Verify ledger integrity
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall verify event sequence continuity, previous hash linkage and record hash recomputation for a project range and append the result as evidence.

provenance.rationale: Integrity claims require independent check evidence.

functional_requirements.title: Correct data through governed supersession
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall support supersession, redaction and tombstone events that reference historical records without mutating original ledger entries.

non_functional_requirements.statement: A governed domain mutation requiring audit shall commit domain state, ledger record and outbox record atomically or commit none of them.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Failure-injection tests interrupt transactions and assert no partial committed combination is visible.
non_functional_requirements.target: Zero partial commit outcomes in the transactional test suite.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Ledger payloads and delivery messages shall be classification-aware, schema-bounded and free of raw secrets and private reasoning.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Security tests submit forbidden payloads and inspect stored/delivered records for redaction and rejection.
non_functional_requirements.target: Zero secret or private-reasoning fields persisted in ledger fixtures.

business_rules.statement: Normal application paths may append and read ledger records but may never update or delete historical ledger entries.
A correction or redaction must append a governed event referencing the original record, applicable policy and authorisation rather than rewriting history.

constraints.statement: The initial ledger supports internal registered producers and consumers only; unreviewed external webhooks and direct third-party event ingestion are excluded.
constraints.rationale: Internal contracts, classification and provenance controls must be proven before external event boundaries are exposed.

dependencies.name: Durable outbox and event delivery runtime
dependencies.risk: Queue/stream selection and operational SLOs remain an ADR decision.

bounded_contexts.name: Audit and Evidence
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Own append-only ledger, evidence records, integrity verification, outbox and projection provenance.

ubiquitous_language.definition: An immutable ordered event envelope in a project partition.
A provenance-backed observed result with exact subject and truth state.
A transactional record awaiting at-least-once delivery to internal consumers.

workflows.name: Append governed domain event
workflows.trigger: A registered domain command commits a material engineering action.

steps.action: Validates event schema, classification, producer authority and payload reference.
steps.result: Invalid records are rejected before append.

steps.action: Atomically writes domain state, ordered ledger record and outbox record.
steps.result: Authoritative action and event have one correlation ID.

steps.action: Verifies requested ledger range or later integrity schedule.
steps.result: Integrity result is stored as evidence.

outcomes: A material action is reconstructable and safely deliverable to projections.
workflows.error_handling: No partial domain/ledger/outbox commit is allowed; delivery failure is retried separately and does not alter ledger state.

security_requirements.statement: Only registered and authenticated internal producers may append permitted event types, and all read queries must enforce project scope and classification.
security_requirements.verification_method: Security tests cover unauthorised producer, wrong event type, non-member query and cross-project access attempts.

observability_requirements.statement: Ledger append, outbox delivery, consumer deduplication, integrity verification and dead-letter outcomes shall emit structured correlated operational events.
observability_requirements.verification_method: Integration tests reconstruct a delivery lifecycle and integrity run from durable records.

acceptance_criteria.title: Domain, ledger and outbox commit atomically
acceptance_criteria.given: An authorised specification command produces a material state change.
acceptance_criteria.then: The domain state, ordered hashed ledger event and outbox record commit together with one correlation ID.

acceptance_criteria.title: Integrity verifier detects continuity and tampering
acceptance_criteria.given: A project ledger range containing valid, gap and altered-record fixtures.
acceptance_criteria.then: It reports verified, gap or mismatch correctly and appends an integrity evidence record.

acceptance_criteria.title: Evidence is versioned and truthful
acceptance_criteria.given: A contract or test result for a specification and implementation revision.
acceptance_criteria.then: The record includes expected/observed result, exact subject versions, artefact hash, provenance, classification and truth status.

acceptance_criteria.title: Consumer de-duplicates delivery
acceptance_criteria.given: An internal consumer receives the same outbox event twice.
acceptance_criteria.then: Projection state changes only once and consumer provenance records the duplicate safely.

acceptance_criteria.title: Redaction preserves audit integrity
acceptance_criteria.given: An authorised policy requires restricted-data correction.
acceptance_criteria.then: It references original event and authority; original ledger integrity remains, while query payload policy redacts protected content.

test_requirements.scope: Atomic domain, ledger and outbox transaction behaviour.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Failure-injection and commit test report with correlation IDs.

test_requirements.scope: Sequence/hash continuity verification and mismatch detection.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Verifier results for valid, missing and altered event fixtures.

test_requirements.scope: Evidence envelope, version references and truth state.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Persisted evidence record fixture linked to exact specification and implementation versions.

test_requirements.scope: At-least-once outbox delivery and idempotent projection consumer.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Duplicate-delivery test report and projection checkpoint record.

test_requirements.scope: Payload policy, classification and governed redaction.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Rejected-secret payload test and redaction-event query test.

risks.title: Ledger payload growth or sensitive-data leakage
risks.description: Unbounded raw event payloads can create cost, performance, privacy and retention failures.
risks.mitigation: Store bounded envelope metadata and artifact hashes/references; enforce classification, schema and redaction policy.

risks.title: Consumers assume exactly-once delivery
risks.description: At-least-once delivery can create duplicate projection state if consumers are not idempotent.
risks.mitigation: Require event-ID deduplication and rebuildable projection provenance.

open_questions.question: Which durable event stream and outbox publisher architecture meets the required ordering, throughput and operational SLOs?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: The production delivery/runtime design cannot be selected.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. Durable stream and outbox runtime selection is a mandatory ADR gate before implementation.

open_questions.question: Which retention, legal-hold and redaction rules apply to each evidence classification?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Evidence storage and privacy correction policy remain incomplete.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. Retention and redaction policy is a mandatory governance gate before production evidence retention.

architecture_decisions.title: Use append-only project hash chains with transactional outbox
architecture_decisions.context: AGASTYA needs reconstructable evidence and reliable internal delivery without depending on mutable logs or distributed transactions.
architecture_decisions.decision: Persist ordered project-scoped ledger records with canonical hash chaining and write an outbox record in the same database transaction as governed domain state.

alternatives.name: Application logs as audit source
alternatives.summary: Use structured logs and external logging service.
alternatives.rejection_reason: Logs are mutable, incomplete and not transactionally coupled to authoritative state.

alternatives.name: Synchronous direct consumer calls
alternatives.summary: Call projection services during the domain transaction.
alternatives.rejection_reason: Creates distributed failure coupling and cannot provide resilient replay.

architecture_decisions.rationale: A ledger/outbox boundary preserves authoritative evidence while allowing resilient at-least-once internal delivery.
consequences: Retention and checkpoint policies require further decisions.

provenance.rationale: Implements immutable audit and evidence primitives from the canonical specification core.
